title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East on 1970-07-12
lineage: all transfers and work performed in the 24 bit realm Weiss-Saracon for 16 BIT 44.1kHz; SBE Free, Flac Level 8 with TLH, Meta Data with Tag & Rename
taper: Mystery Reel of an unknown audience recording uncovered  and shared by LL member Cloverman, which he sent to Matt Smith for his great reel transfer work.  The handwriting on the reel case is thought to be Latvala's, no more is known.

ai_review.summary: Acoustic gems like Attics and a first‑ever How Long Blues shine despite the tape‑grade (C) sound quality.
ai_review.review: The recording captures an intimate acoustic set that builds to a thrilling finish with Attics and a rare How Long Blues, which many reviewers call “off the charts.”  The audio is described as a definite C – likely cassette‑type fidelity – so while the performance shines, the technical side feels modest.

ai_rating.rationale: Both reviewers are enthusiastic about the music (high show quality) but note low‑fidelity sound, leading to a strong overall rating tempered by recording limitations.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewer calls the sound a “definite C,” indicating modest fidelity typical of tape or low‑grade audience recordings; no major dropouts reported.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Acoustic set builds smoothly to a powerful climax, highlighted by an ecstatic dancing finale.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Mentioned singing “don’t murder me” in the anecdotal memory; no specific instrumental critique.
